items.text: An anti-Iranian statement by a broadcaster about sacrificing southern Iran for southern Lebanon sparked a campaign on social media. Young people from the 80s and 90s generations responded with a song by the Sandy group and images of Reza Shah's armbands. Aryan Risbaf reported on this issue.

Abolfazl Shekarchi, senior spokesperson of Iran's armed forces, placed employees of Iran International, BBC Persian, and Radio Farda in a 'military target bank.' He called these employees 'soldiers of Israel and America.' This threat follows ongoing pressure by the Islamic Republic against journalists abroad.

Bloomberg, citing three informed individuals, reported that the US Department of Justice is creating a court to facilitate the military seizure of Iranian oil tankers and taking them as prize. Aaron Reitz, the US Attorney for the Southern District of Texas, confirmed that the DOJ is reviving 'prize courts' and his office is cooperating. According to Bloomberg, this court could provide the necessary legal framework for handling tankers seized by the US in military operations.
Real Madrid defeated Real Sociedad 4-1 in the postponed first week match of La Liga. Kylian Mbappe scored a hat-trick and Vinicius Junior scored one goal. Jude Bellingham provided two assists.

Abolfazl Shekarchi, the spokesperson for the armed forces, called journalists and staff of Iran International, BBC, Manoto, and Radio Farda "Zionist soldiers" and "soldiers of criminal America." He described these networks as hostile and warmongering and said the armed forces consider them in their military target bank. He also claimed these networks are directly connected to Mossad and the CIA and receive guidance from them.

According to Nepal police, at least 160 people died in a sudden flood on Wednesday in the Nepal-China border area. More than 400 tourists, workers, and other citizens are missing. In Mailong, some people escaped the flood path moments before it arrived.

Morad Veysi stated that the severe gasoline shortage in Tehran and other provinces is causing more gas stations to close daily. He described this crisis as a time bomb under the Islamic Republic. He also said that the government has lost the ability to control these crises.

Masoud Pezeshkian referred to foreign interference and said the enemy wants to create discord among Islamic Republic officials. He added that the enemy's goal is to engage them in character assassination against each other.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that the combination of increasing crises and the Islamic Republic's inability to control them has put society in a state of pre-uprising. He warned that the risk of the situation going out of government control and the collapse of the regime has increased.
Qalibaf stated that talking with Washington is not taboo amid tensions at the highest levels of government over negotiations with the US. He defended negotiating with the United States.

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, announced the construction of three stadiums with capacities between 40,000 and 60,000 in Tehran. He also requested that the renovation of the Azadi Stadium be assigned to the municipality. The Minister of Sports stated that building large stadiums is not currently a government priority, but acknowledged the municipality's efforts.

The Minister of Communications admitted that about 100,000 Starlink devices have entered Iran. He acknowledged that the government has failed to prevent people's access to social networks. He also said that the expansion of satellite internet will further reduce the Islamic Republic's control over the communication space.

Jamshid Barzegar said that in the absence of Mojtaba Khamenei, key decisions in the Islamic Republic have been handed over to a core group close to the Revolutionary Guards. He added that statements by Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf indicate increasing tensions among these factions. The continued absence of Mojtaba Khamenei has also increased ambiguity about the real decision-making authority in the Islamic Republic.

Amir Giti from Iran International said mutual distrust between the Islamic Republic, the IAEA, and Western countries has complicated inspectors' access to nuclear facilities. He added that Iran's concern about information leaking to the US and Israel is more of a leverage tactic in future negotiations. This issue stems from internal disagreements and mutual distrust.
Bank Melli has confirmed disruptions and discrepancies in some accounts. Transaction corrections and balance updates are ongoing. Customers complain about not having access to their account balances.

During a parliamentary energy commission meeting to investigate the causes of nationwide power outages, the electricity went out. This incident is seen as a bitter irony in the Islamic Republic. The topic was discussed by Kambiz Hosseini in a program.

The United States is reviewing the deployment of its forces in Europe and has asked European countries to take primary responsibility for their own defense. This move follows Trump's criticism of European countries for not doing more to assist the US in the war with the Islamic Republic. European diplomats are trying to assure the Pentagon that they are increasing their defense activities.

Anna Kelly, the principal deputy White House spokesperson, stated that there are no ongoing or planned negotiations with the Islamic Republic. Donald Trump also said there is no specific timeline for resuming talks and he is in no hurry. Trump added that both military attacks and economic pressure by the US against the Islamic Republic have been effective.

Bloomberg reported, citing officials, that a number of US allies believe the Strait of Hormuz has not yet been fully demined. These sources estimated the number of mines laid by the Islamic Republic at around 80 to 150, but the exact number of remaining mines is unknown. This assessment contradicts statements by Donald Trump about the waterway's clearance.

Scott Perry, a Republican member of the US House of Representatives, said the Islamic Republic should not be allowed to obtain nuclear weapons. He added that Donald Trump seeks to end the conflict quickly. These remarks follow the Trump administration's stance on Iran's nuclear program.

Meta has reached a settlement of up to $18 billion with 48 US states over allegations that Instagram and Facebook are addictive for children. This agreement halts several ongoing trials, and Meta is required to implement new protective measures for children and teenagers. However, thousands of individuals and hundreds of school districts still have complaints against Meta and other social media networks.

Nepalese officials initially attributed the deadly flood to an earthquake, but studies indicate a landslide of rock and ice blocked a river. The breaking of this natural dam caused a devastating wave of water and mud, killing at least 160 people and leaving hundreds missing. Experts have not yet confirmed a definite link between this disaster and climate change.

A Politico report shows bipartisan support in the US Congress for sanctioning Chinese banks that assist Iran's financial flow has increased. These sanctions could have broad consequences for the global financial system. Concerns about China's possible retaliatory response have also been raised.

Washington Stand, a conservative American media, analyzed threats by Barron Trump and an alleged attempt to kill one of Netanyahu's sons as reflecting the Islamic Republic's view of political leaders' families. It highlighted the role of family loyalty in the power structure of the Islamic Republic. The analysis also compared this with the influence of political families in the US.

The US Navy plans to deploy the aircraft carrier Theodore Roosevelt with five thousand crew members on a seven-month mission to the Middle East, which may extend to eight months. This carrier will replace the USS George Washington and will depart from San Diego. The average deployment duration of US aircraft carriers has increased to eight and a half months.

Miad Maleki stated that reviving maritime prize courts could allow the US Department of Justice to seize oil tankers and cargo related to the Islamic Republic. He added that this could severely impact shipping companies and the network circumventing sanctions. Seizing a few ships could result in the loss of hundreds of millions of dollars in assets.

Kayhan newspaper wrote that the steadfastness of the Iranian people and armed forces has caused the White House to return to the cycle of sanctions. Kayhan stated that Tehran is changing the rules of the game and will target US positions in the region. The newspaper warned that if sanctions continue, the US must bear the heavy costs of insecurity in the region.

Mehrdad Ghasemfar commented on Trump's statements about Mojtaba Khamenei's health, saying the main issue is his ability to lead the Islamic Republic. He added that if Mojtaba Khamenei cannot play the role of arbitrator for Ali Khamenei, the Islamic Republic will face a serious existential crisis.

Arash Yazdani Hemmatabadi was shot by Khamenei's forces on January 8th at Haft-Hovz Square in Tehran. This event is recorded in the context of the Iranian National Revolution. His memory remains a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Shahram Khaledi said that Donald Trump's strategic ambiguity allowed him to shift the playing field against the Islamic Republic. He used military, economic, and diplomatic tools to increase the cost of the regime's survival. This is an analysis of Trump's policy towards Iran.

The 20-year vision document of the Islamic Republic of Iran, announced 22 years ago by Ali Khamenei, has expired. This document has become a symbol of the failure of Khamenei's policies. Ali Khamenei has also passed away during this period.

Gila Gamliel, Israel's Minister of Innovation, said that Prince Reza Pahlavi will return to power in Iran and will be welcomed with royal splendor. She added that this event will happen soon and by God's will. Gamliel also emphasized continuing the fight against the Islamic Republic until the regime is overthrown.

Mehdi Beigi from Iran International reported that the IRGC opposes the government's unlimited withdrawal from strategic gasoline reserves. The government has made contradictory statements about fuel status, with a daily gasoline deficit of about 15 million liters. The reserves may run out in a few weeks, and the government is considering options such as limiting supply and raising prices.

US lawmakers from both parties have asked the Trump administration to sanction Chinese banks facilitating Iran's oil trade. Beijing called these pressures illegal and warned of retaliatory measures. These tensions have increased ahead of the US-China presidential meeting.

Iraj Masjedi stated that the Islamic Republic forces should not wait for the enemy to reach Iran's borders and must act preventively. He said the presence of Islamic Republic forces in Lebanon, Iraq, Syria, and other countries aims to prevent threats from approaching Iran's borders. He also mentioned that forces from Afghanistan, Pakistan, Iraq, Lebanon, Palestine, and Yemen are present in what the Islamic Republic calls the resistance front.

Roozbeh Sinky, a former goalkeeper, criticized the economic and livelihood situation of the people in a note. He pointed to discrimination, oppression, poverty, and livelihood problems, stating that people do not have basic citizenship rights. Sinky had previously been arrested for supporting people's protests.

Politico, citing informed sources, reported that CIA Director John Ratcliffe, during an unannounced trip to Moscow, asked Russian officials to reduce military and economic support for the Islamic Republic. Ratcliffe requested a halt to the supply of weapons and defense technologies to Iran. An informed British official said Ratcliffe also asked Moscow not to 'overreact' if US sanctions affect Russia.

Mehdi Savaraliyah was sentenced to six years in prison and additional penalties. He was convicted of propaganda against the regime and conspiracy against national security. He is also banned from leaving the country and joining social groups.

Drivers at a fuel station in Fardis, Karaj protested by honking due to gasoline shortage and long waiting times. A citizen reported this protest to Iran International. A video of the protest was sent.
Mansour Karbalaei, a citizen from Miandoab, was arrested on Tuesday to serve a prison sentence of 10 years and one day. He was transferred to Bukan prison.

Mojtaba Khamenei has been absent from the public eye in recent weeks and has not released any new messages or statements. This has sparked questions and humor on social media. Users have noted the halt in his message releases and linked it to possible use of artificial intelligence.

Reports have been published about the sharp increase in prices in Iran. Daily expenses such as medicine, food, and car services have risen significantly. Additionally, tuition fees for private schools and educational costs have also increased greatly.

An eyewitness reported that some gas stations in the capital are out of gasoline and people are told there is no fuel. However, vehicles and motorcycles of the special unit easily refuel at Takhti gas station. This situation has also been observed in the Hijrat highway area.

The CEO of Golestan Water and Wastewater Company announced that 257 villages are supplied with water by tanker continuously or during water stress periods. Out of 30 tankers, 25 are over 21 years old. An emergency water supply plan requires 1,336 billion tomans in funding.

Mehdi Mohammadi, strategic advisor to Qalibaf, said neighboring countries will not comply with sanctions as the US wants. He added that price increases are due to people's emotional behaviors and are not related to US sanctions.

The Bank Melli branch in Hamburg remains active despite EU sanctions. The German government spokesperson confirmed the bank is subject to extensive sanctions. German regulatory bodies have not provided clear responses regarding the enforcement of these sanctions.

The director of education in Babol announced that 23 schools in the county are damaged and need reconstruction. Among them, 12 schools are in urban areas and 11 in rural areas. The extent of damage to these schools is estimated to be between 20 to 100 percent.

A citizen showed in a video to Iran International that he lit his house with candles and lanterns during a power outage. He compared the current situation to the "Stone Age." The citizen held the Islamic Republic responsible for this situation.

An indictment has been issued for a man accused of killing his wife and 13-year-old daughter in Tehran. The case has been sent to Branch 10 of the Criminal Court One of Tehran Province. The accused is charged with shooting them.

The German federal government spokesperson stated that Berlin is in contact with the US and European partners regarding further actions against the Islamic Republic. The National Bank branch in Hamburg continues its daily operations. The German financial supervisory authority has not made a specific statement about the bank's status.

The Israeli army announced that it killed two important members of Hamas's military wing named Rizq Suhail Suleiman and Hazem Mousa. These individuals were involved in planning actions against military forces and civilians. It was also stated that they violated the ceasefire.
A truck driver criticized the long queues for diesel fuel in a video shared on social media. He said that a large part of drivers' time is wasted waiting in these queues to receive fuel.
The public prosecutor of Tabas announced the closure of two commercial units due to publishing content against decency and legal regulations in cyberspace.

In Tehran and Karaj, a shortage of gasoline has caused long queues at gas stations. Some stations have no gasoline, and the gasoline quota for foreign cars has been cut. The shortage has also reached the city of Sarab in East Azerbaijan.

Rafael Grossi, Director General of the IAEA, stated that Iran's nuclear negotiations have stopped. He said the nuclear file is a second priority until the situation in the Strait of Hormuz is clarified. The agency is ready to resume its activities in Iran, but no progress has been seen in the talks.

Esteghlal club announced that its home matches in the Asian Elite League will be held in Basra, Iraq. Esteghlal will host Al Sadd and Al Shamal from Qatar, Neftchi from Uzbekistan, and Al Wasl from the UAE in this stadium. This decision was made due to political conditions and security considerations.

Safwat Raslan, Governor of the Central Bank of Syria, posted a video on X showing President Ahmed al-Sharaa paying for his coffee with a Visa card at a café in central Damascus. The action is considered the first international Visa card payment in the country. The event took place one day after the United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism, a list Syria had been on since 1979.

Abdollah Naseri wrote a letter calling Mojtaba Khamenei the probable leader of the Islamic Republic and emphasized the need to transition from the religious government. Morteza Kazemian pointed to doubts about Mojtaba Khamenei's condition and the possibility of the Revolutionary Guards controlling the leadership. The letter raises concerns about the future of leadership and the system of velayat-e faqih.

Football360 published a video of a southern fan who was prevented from entering the Sirous Ghayegharan Stadium in Anzali because he was wearing shorts. The fan ultimately had to change his clothes to watch the match between Malavan and Fajr Sepasi.

Leila Morvati said the Qatari foreign minister's visit to Tehran and mediation by Qatar and Pakistan could facilitate diplomacy. She added that differences within the Islamic Republic make a quick return to negotiations unlikely. She also emphasized that the military option remains alongside economic and diplomatic pressure by the US.
Aram News reported that European countries have provided confidential information to the US about tracking Iranian money abroad. This was detailed in a report by Sadaf Baghbani on Iran International.

A citizen in Mashhad reported an increase in the presence of armed groups and black-clad motorcyclists in Vakilabad and Ahmadabad boulevards. These forces are stationed on the streets from the evening and are sensitive to filming. The created atmosphere was described as similar to an undeclared martial law.

People report shortages of infant formula and special hearing aids in the market. Medical and school registration costs have increased significantly. Additionally, issues such as slow internet speed and high prices of household items have been reported.

The 12th National Festival of Song and Dance "Gusan" has started in the capital of Armenia. The festival will be held for one month in various parts of the country. It features performances of traditional Armenian music and local dances.

Twelve plainclothes agents from the Ministry of Intelligence raided the house of Vahid Moghann in Isfahan. Sarir Moghann was arrested after several hours of search and transferred to Dolatabad prison. Many items including electronics, money, gold, and wedding rings were confiscated.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, met with Abbas Araghchi in Tehran to discuss regional developments and ways to reduce tensions. They reviewed a phased proposal for the Strait of Hormuz, including a joint passage route for ships and a mine-clearing project. Al Thani emphasized respecting neighboring countries' sovereignty and freedom of navigation.

Leila Abolhasani, a 43-year-old prisoner, has been sentenced to death for moharebeh by the Revolutionary Court of Isfahan. The verdict was issued by the fifth branch of the court and the case has been sent to the Supreme Court for appeal. Her charge is related to the December protests and the burning of a chain store.

A citizen reported in a video that the nighttime gasoline queue on Damavand Street in Tehran extended from fuel station 104 to Dariush station. This report was sent to Iran International. The situation of gasoline queues in this area was shown live.

One day after the devastating flood in Nepal, search operations with helicopters continue. At least 350 people have died and more than 900 are missing. Experts believe the flood was caused by the detachment of part of a glacier and a massive avalanche.

A suicide drone was destroyed on Wednesday evening in the Soran district of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. The drone's crash caused a widespread forest fire. The Kurdistan Region's Prime Minister condemned the attacks by the Islamic Republic and called on the US to assist in strengthening air defense.

Esteghlal Club has chosen Basra International Stadium in Iraq as the venue for its home matches in the AFC Champions League. The Iraqi Football Federation has signed the hosting contract and the stadium documents have been sent to the Asian Football Confederation. If approved, Esteghlal will host teams Al Sadd, Al Shamal, Neftchi, and Al Wasl.

Cristiano Ronaldo tops the list of highest-paid players in the Saudi league with a weekly salary of 4 million euros. He is also the highest-paid football player in the world. Ronaldo won the championship with Al Nassr last season and is now preparing to defend the title.

Ahmad Alavi, an economist, warned about the sharp increase in transportation costs and taxi fares. He identified fuel shortages and price hikes as causes of a spiral inflation and reduced household purchasing power. This situation may lead to increased poverty.

A men's clothing store in Dezful was closed due to producing and publishing inappropriate content on social media. The store manager was arrested and his case was referred to the judiciary. This was announced by the Dezful county police commander.

A citizen criticized the high prices of eggs and oil in a video sent to Iran International. He cursed the founder of the Islamic Republic and the revolutionaries of 1979. This video has been publicly shared.

Manouchehr Motaki said that if the US does not implement the agreement, Iran should not give Trump an advantage. He emphasized that it is time for action and that the US has rejected negotiations with the Islamic Republic. He also mentioned that if Trump loses the US midterm elections, there will be two years of confusion, but if he wins, Israel will push them towards war.

The Director General of Urban Environmental Improvement of Mashhad Municipality announced a ban on dog walking in the city's parks. This directive has been communicated to the 13 municipal districts. Over 200 informational signs about this ban have been installed in Mashhad's parks.

Michel Aoun, the US ambassador to Lebanon, said Hezbollah receives its orders only from the Islamic Republic. He added that Lebanese people agree on disarming Hezbollah. He also emphasized that Hezbollah takes no action against Israeli attacks.

Mohsen Namjoo announced that after about 20 years, he is on the way back to Iran. He said it does not matter to him whether he has musical or cultural activities in Iran and he wants to be with his family and friends. He also planned to hold concerts in Toronto, Washington DC, and New York.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the farewell ceremony of new ambassadors that the Islamic Republic's approach in international relations is peaceful and interaction-oriented. He emphasized that countries' interests should be met through interaction without greed. The new ambassadors must accurately explain this approach to the people of the world.

Leila Abolhasani, detained during the January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to death on charges of moharebeh. Her case is currently under review by the Supreme Court following an appeal. She has been held in Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan since January 8, 2026.

Kaveh Madani, an Iranian water researcher, received the 2026 Stockholm Water Prize from the King of Sweden. The award was given in recognition of his research and activities in water resource management and governance. The prize includes one million Swedish kronor and a crystal trophy.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, criticized the Islamic Republic's financial policies in a post on X, calling for the country's financial resources to be allocated to the Iranian people. He said that instead of injecting billions of dollars into its terrorist proxy groups, the Iranian government should spend this money on its own people. These remarks come amid intensified US financial sanctions against Iran.

Asieh Ramazani, a 39-year-old woman and mother of two, was killed by direct gunfire from the Islamic Republic forces during the suppression of the December 1404 protests in Tehran. Her family criticized the handling of her body and the failure to return her personal belongings. They emphasize that the full circumstances of her death remain unclear.

Ahmad Zeraatkar stated that 40% of the damaged capacity of South Pars has returned to production. Deputy Paknejad said the debris removal of South Pars has been completed. Reconstruction is being carried out in an organized and planned manner.

The Pentagon has prepared a plan to review the US military presence in Europe. This plan is set to be presented to the US Secretary of Defense next month. Some European officials are concerned about a possible reduction of the US military presence in Europe.

A citizen criticized the high cost of medicine in a video sent to Iran International. He said the treatment cost for a simple cold is nearly three million tomans. This issue highlights patients' concerns.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, stated that any dialogue must be conducted from a position of strength and with acceptance of the realities on the ground. He emphasized that the confrontation with the enemy is not only military but also includes economic, cultural, social, media, diplomatic, and psychological arenas.

Mediators from Qatar, Oman, and Pakistan are trying to restore the Strait of Hormuz to normal conditions and start negotiations with the US. However, there is a significant gap between the Islamic Republic's demands and Washington's position. Continued economic pressure could reduce the Islamic Republic's ability to meet essential needs.

Caroline Lewitt, White House spokesperson, stated that currently there are no negotiations between the United States and the Islamic Republic. She emphasized that all options regarding the Islamic Republic remain on Donald Trump's table. These remarks were made in an interview with Fox News.

The mayor of Sanandaj announced that about 55% of the city's urban fabric is in inefficient or worn-out areas. Informal settlements and ownership issues have challenged safe urban development. Additionally, the average age of the municipality's construction machinery has reached 38 to 40 years.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, met with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Tehran. They discussed regional developments and efforts to reduce tensions. The Qatari Foreign Minister stated that dialogue is the best way to resolve disputes.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, met with Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Iranian government, in Tehran. He also met with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Iranian Parliament, to discuss solutions for resuming negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

Mojtaba Khamenei has been introduced as the third leader of the Islamic Republic but has not appeared in public or been heard. This absence may indicate the government's weakness or delay the political death of the Islamic Republic. Previously, the regime displayed its leaders everywhere, but now it releases messages from the new leader without showing him.

Hamidreza Amiri denied the accusations made by his wife Vida Rabani regarding domestic violence and property seizure. He stated that his wife's account is fundamentally incorrect and does not match the facts and documents. Amiri asked the audience to review the narratives and evidence from both sides.

Majid Bahiraei, a political prisoner and detainee from the December 1404 protests, is serving his sentence in Malayer prison. He was sentenced to two years and two months of imprisonment by Branch 101 of the Nahavand Revolutionary Court. This information was confirmed by a source close to his family.

Hojatollah Nikimaleki has been appointed as the chairman of Digikala's board. He previously managed the media of the Execution of Imam Khomeini's Order and the Afseran social network. This news was published by Iran International.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, the Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar, met with Masoud Pezeshkian during his visit to Tehran. He also discussed the resumption of negotiations between Washington and Tehran with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. The Qatari foreign minister emphasized that dialogue is the best way to resolve disputes and prevent further escalation of tensions.

Le Monde reported that Persian Gulf countries, after six months of intense tension between Tehran and Washington, are trying to reduce their dependence on the Strait of Hormuz for oil exports by building and developing pipelines. The UAE is expanding its Habshan to Fujairah pipeline to reach a capacity of about 3.6 million barrels per day.
The World Humanoid Robot Competition in Beijing ended after five days of contests. Robots set new records in sports and practical skills. Their unexpected movements amazed the spectators.
Elham Khalas, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Isfahan, was arrested after appearing at the General and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of the city. She was transferred to Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan.

The Intelligence Organization of the IRGC stated that the Islamic Republic has moved beyond mere survival and is now stabilizing its resilience. It is not only responding to attacks but increasing its strategic initiative. Military readiness to deliver a decisive blow to the enemy is one of its key activities.

Citizens report a sharp increase in the prices of baby formula, medical costs, and school tuition. Snapp drivers complain about technical issues and reduced income. Additionally, internet outages have caused programmers to lose their jobs.

Mohsen Rezaei warned the US that if it initiates hostility against the Islamic Republic, it will face severe consequences for its military and economic interests. He emphasized that the US must first fulfill the Islamic Republic's conditions before Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz. Rezaei also stated that they do not trust the US, which has repeatedly betrayed diplomacy.

Israel Hayom newspaper wrote that Israel must remain prepared for the scenario of renewed direct conflict with the Islamic Republic. The newspaper emphasized that economic pressures and sanctions, while limiting Tehran's financial resources, are not sufficient alone to change the Islamic Republic's policies. The report was by Babak Es-haqi from Iran International.

Reports indicate fuel shortages and long queues at gas stations. At the same time, the atmosphere in some Iranian cities has become highly securitized. This information comes from public reports received by Iran International.

David Barnea, former Mossad chief, said Donald Trump understands that the Iranian regime should not be allowed to remain in power. He described the severe sanctions against the Islamic Republic as a correct but only one step. Barnea called for intensifying economic, diplomatic, and operational measures against the Iranian regime until its fall.

On the morning of Wednesday, 5 Shahrivar, part of a glacier in the Himalayas collapsed, causing a deadly flood. The incident resulted in at least 165 deaths and over a thousand missing people. Scientists are still investigating the exact cause of this disaster.
In a village in Sabzevar, Khorasan Razavi, citizens have written protest slogans and support for the Pahlavi family on the walls. This was reported through videos sent to Iran International.

Associated Press reported that about 65% of the US Patriot interceptor missiles have been used in the war with the Islamic Republic. This equals approximately 1,500 out of a total of 2,330 missiles. The US interceptor missile stocks in Europe have reached a critical level.

Donald Trump stated that Russia has behaved very well regarding the Strait of Hormuz. He also said Vladimir Putin will not attack NATO territory. Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario to 'Lake America'.

In recent years, the criminal responsibility of business owners for customers' behavior has increased. This issue is used as a tool for social control, and even without direct involvement, the business owner may be punished. This approach challenges criminal law principles because criminal responsibility should be personal, and ownership or management alone does not create liability.
Donald Trump said that they moved 24 vessels through the Strait of Hormuz last night and do this regularly. He added that this does not mean the military mission is over.

The family of Lindsay and Craig Foreman has asked the British government to arrange consular visits and check their health status. Despite the return of British embassy staff to Tehran, no consular meeting has taken place yet. Joe Bennet was able to speak with his mother by phone for the first time in three months.

A US source stated that any agreement between the Islamic Republic and Oman is not important to Washington. It was also said that the Strait of Hormuz is open and mines have been cleared. Currently, no negotiations with Tehran are ongoing or planned.

Ali Rasoulnejad, a resident of Mahabad, was arrested by the Intelligence Force of the IRGC. He was detained yesterday and transferred to an unknown location. No further details about his situation have been released.

Abbas Araghchi stated that the Islamic Republic is sincerely implementing its commitments under the ceasefire agreement, but the US has disrupted the process by violating the agreement. He also said that the situation in the Strait of Hormuz cannot return to its state before March 2026 without considering the damages to Iran. These remarks were made during a meeting with his Qatari counterpart.
The VIP cafe in Tehran was closed by relevant authorities due to mandatory hijab issues. This action was reported by Harana News Agency. More details are provided in the continuation of the report.

The 40th-day memorial ceremony for Aref Khoshkar was held in Behesht Zahra, Tehran, attended by his family and citizens. Aref Khoshkar was one of the detainees of the 2022 nationwide protests. He was executed in July of this year in Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the 21st Rajai Festival that our country is a victim of terror. He said either people are turned against each other or direct attacks occur. Pezeshkian added that the mistake is distancing from the people.

The Intelligence Organization of the IRGC warned about increasing social dissatisfaction and the possibility of street protests. It claimed that the opponents of the Islamic Republic have changed their strategy to activating internal crises and psychological warfare. It also alleged the identification of a secret Mossad structure operating inside Iran.

Donald Trump signed an executive order to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America. This decision was made following trade tensions between the US and Canada. Canadian officials have stated they will not recognize this name change.

Hassan Bandani, a 21-year-old auto body worker from Shahin Shahr, Isfahan, was arrested on July 19 after going to the Execution of Sentences Office at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan and was transferred to solitary confinement. He was detained due to his participation in the December protests and causing disorder. Bandani remains in solitary confinement without access to a lawyer or phone.

The Trump administration has stated it does not wish to return to the terms of the initial June agreement with the Islamic Republic. This stance has hindered efforts by Qatar, Oman, and Pakistan to revive negotiations between Washington and Tehran. The White House has announced that no negotiations with the Islamic Republic are underway and that the naval blockade and economic exclusion operations will continue.

Mohsen Rezaei stated that if the blockade continues, the economic interests of the United States will be targeted 100%. He said that if fighting resumes, future wars will be different. Rezaei also announced the breaking of the naval blockade and the return of oil sales to pre-sanction levels.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, threatened Benjamin Netanyahu with death and said Netanyahu's mistakes have brought the end of Israel's existence closer. Rezaee denied the claim that the Islamic Republic planned to kill Donald Trump and his son, calling it a big lie. He also stated that if the Islamic Republic decides to take action, nothing will prevent it.

Ahmad Donyamali stated that he is trying to create an opportunity for Chadormalu to represent Iran in the next season of the AFC Champions League. He mentioned that this issue is one of the reasons for his impeachment and emphasized not to accuse the Minister of Sports of corruption. Previously, the impeachment reasons included administrative corruption and poor international performance.

Thomas Juneau stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains a major concern for the US and that the Islamic Republic can endure economic pressures in the short and medium term. He added that both sides are currently unwilling to resume direct war, but the situation is fragile. Despite damage to its military capabilities, the Islamic Republic still retains the ability to target the Strait of Hormuz and regional infrastructure.

Mohsen Namjoo returned to Iran after about 29 years living abroad. He stated that he might resume his artistic activities and stage performances. The Minister of Culture also mentioned reviewing the possibility of the return of over 100 Iranian figures living abroad.
